what: Essex Property Trust owns apartment buildings on the US West Coast, concentrated in Southern California, the San Francisco Bay Area and Seattle. It owns and manages the buildings itself.
customers: Apartment renters in West Coast metropolitan areas, typically on one-year leases.
moat: Buildings in coastal markets where land is scarce and planning rules are restrictive, so very little new supply is added even when rents rise.
risks: Debt of about $6.4 billion against almost no cash
West Coast technology employment drives demand and has been uneven
Rent control and tenant protection rules in California limit increases
opportunities: Operating margin of 48% and net margin of 35%
Almost no new apartment supply is under construction in its markets
A dividend yield near 4% raised every year for three decades
watch: Same-property revenue growth and occupancy on the West Coast.
